strategies.name: Buy locally, collect in person
strategies.summary: Always check this first. A €40 fridge in Braga beats a €25 fridge in Bavaria every single time once you price the movement.
steps: Search OLX.pt and CustoJusto.pt before anything else.
Meet in a public place; pay on collection after testing the item.

strategies.name: Platform's own cross-border shipping
strategies.summary: Vinted, eBay International Shipping and OLX Envios handle the label, the customs paperwork (none, inside the EU) and the dispute process themselves. Buyer Protection means a non-delivery is a refund, not a fight.
steps: Filter results to listings whose platform ships to PT (the "ships to PT" toggle).
Pay in-app; never move the conversation off-platform, or protection lapses.

strategies.name: Send the seller a prepaid label
strategies.summary: The single highest-leverage trick in this whole tool. You buy the cross-border label yourself on a broker, email the seller a PDF or QR code, and they drop the parcel at a shop 300m away. The seller pays nothing, does no paperwork and takes no risk — which is why sellers who "don't ship abroad" almost always say yes to this. Brokers resell carrier contracts at 30-60% below counter rates.
steps: Agree the sale and get the parcel's real dimensions and weight from the seller.
Buy the label on Packlink / Sendcloud / Eurosender for the seller's address → yours.
Email the PDF label + QR and the nearest drop-off point (link them the map).
Pay only after you have the tracking number showing "accepted at drop-off".
caveats: Never send the label before the seller has confirmed the sale in writing.
Insure above €100 of value; broker default cover is usually €25.

strategies.name: InPost locker-to-locker (Poland corridor)
strategies.summary: Poland is the EU's best-value market for used electronics, tools and photo gear, and it is also the one with the slickest logistics: OLX Przesyłki runs on InPost Paczkomaty, and InPost now operates lockers in Portugal. Seller walks to a locker, you collect from a locker. No one waits in a queue.
steps: Buy via OLX Przesyłki where the listing offers it.
Otherwise generate an InPost international label and send it to the seller.

strategies.name: Packeta / Zásilkovna to a Portuguese pickup point
strategies.summary: Central Europe's answer to InPost. Bazoš and Jófogás sellers know Packeta the way German sellers know DHL, and Packeta delivers to Portuguese pickup points — so the whole thing stays inside a workflow the seller already uses.
steps: Ask the seller to send "Packeta / Zásilkovna do zahraničí" to your PT pickup point.
Or buy the label yourself on packeta.com and send it over.

strategies.name: Spanish border pickup (drive across)
strategies.summary: Portugal's only land border is with the EU's second-largest second-hand market, and Spanish domestic shipping is both cheap and universally offered. Have the seller ship *domestically* to a Correos office or locker in a border town, then collect by car. For anything bulky — furniture, bikes, appliances — this is dramatically cheaper than international freight, and the "fixed_extra" below is roughly a tank of fuel and tolls.
steps: Ask the seller for plain Correos/SEUR domestic shipping (they will not object — it is normal for them).
Ship to "Correos Oficina" list-of-post in Tui (Galicia, ~30min from Valença), Badajoz (~15min from Elvas), Ayamonte (~10min from Vila Real de Santo António), or Vigo/Salamanca for larger depots.
Collect with passport; Correos holds parcels 15 days.
caveats: You need a Spanish address line the seller accepts — a Correos office address works.
Batch several purchases into one trip or the fuel eats the saving.

strategies.name: Spanish forwarding address + consolidation
strategies.summary: Same idea as border pickup without the drive: rent a Spanish address, have several sellers ship domestically to it, then have the forwarder consolidate everything into one box for Portugal. Consolidation is where the money is — four separate €9 domestic parcels become one €18 international one.
steps: Open an account with a Spanish forwarder or a Correos "Apartado" box.
Give sellers the Spanish address; wait for everything to land.
Request consolidation, then one shipment to PT.

strategies.name: German forwarding address (for DE-only sellers)
strategies.summary: Germany has the deepest pool of used goods in Europe and the most rigid "Versand nur innerhalb Deutschlands" culture. A German forwarding address dissolves that entirely: the seller posts a normal domestic DHL parcel, the forwarder inspects it (worth paying for on Kleinanzeigen buys) and reships to Portugal.
steps: Register with a German forwarder and get your personal DE address.
Buy as a domestic German buyer; pay the seller by SEPA transfer.
Request photos/inspection on arrival before paying for the onward leg.
caveats: Forwarders charge storage after ~30 days; consolidate promptly.

strategies.name: Portuguese diaspora van (carrinha de emigrantes)
strategies.summary: The genuinely unconventional one, and for heavy or bulky goods from France, Luxembourg, Switzerland or Germany it beats every courier by a wide margin. Dozens of small Portuguese transport firms run weekly vans along the emigration corridors, door to door, priced by volume rather than by chargeable weight. They will happily take a washing machine, a motorbike fairing or six boxes of books. France is by far the densest corridor.
steps: Search "transporte de encomendas França Portugal" or "carrinhas para Portugal" plus your region; most operators live on Facebook groups rather than websites.
Agree pickup at the seller's address and delivery to yours; confirm the week's run.
Pay part on pickup, remainder on delivery. Get the driver's phone number and plate.
caveats: Informal sector — no tracking, no insurance, schedules slip by days.
Only use an operator with a real trading history and reviews you can read.
Never for high-value electronics; ideal for bulky, low-value-density goods.

strategies.name: Coach and bus parcel service
strategies.summary: Long-distance coach operators sell hold space as parcel freight, station to station. Cheap, fast for the Iberian corridor, and takes odd-shaped items couriers refuse. You collect from the bus station.
steps: Ask the seller to drop the parcel at their local coach station office.
Collect at Lisboa Sete Rios, Porto Campanhã or your regional terminal.

strategies.name: Palletised road freight
strategies.summary: For furniture, machine tools, engines and anything a parcel carrier will refuse. A half-pallet from Germany to Portugal is €120-200 — absurd for a €60 chair, excellent for a €900 lathe or a set of Vitra chairs.
steps: Get exact dimensions and weight; have the seller palletise and wrap it.
Book through a freight broker; specify a tail-lift if there is no loading dock.

strategies.name: Traveller crowdshipping
strategies.summary: Platforms that match your parcel with a traveller already making the trip. Realistically a niche play: matching is slow and depends entirely on someone happening to fly your route. Worth a try for small, high-value, hard-to-ship items — and for anything a courier would classify as dangerous goods (lithium batteries, aerosols, some tools).
steps: Post the route and wait for a carrier match; verify their ID and reviews.
Use the platform's escrow. Never pay a carrier directly.
caveats: You are trusting a stranger with the goods; keep value low.

strategies.name: Hand-carry on a flight
strategies.summary: A 23kg hold bag on a Ryanair or easyJet leg into Lisboa or Porto costs €40-60 flat and has no per-kilo penalty at all. If you, a friend or a family member is already flying that route, it is the cheapest way to move anything dense and valuable — camera gear, lenses, tools, vinyl. Ship the item to their local address first via cheap domestic post.
steps: Have the seller ship domestically to your contact in-country.
Add a hold bag to their existing booking.
Keep lithium batteries in the cabin, not the hold — airline rules, not a suggestion.

strategies.name: In-country proxy buyer / inspection
strategies.summary: For high-value buys on platforms with no buyer protection — Kleinanzeigen, Bazoš, SS.lv — the real risk is not shipping, it is that the item is not what the photos claim. Someone local who can meet the seller, test the item and pay cash converts a stranger-danger transaction into a normal one, then reships domestically. Costs a favour or a small fee; saves entire purchases.
steps: Find a local contact, an expat forum member, or a paid inspection service.
They meet, test, pay cash, then ship domestically or via prepaid label.
caveats: Only worth the coordination above roughly €300 of item value.
